reviews.reason: The corrected scalar-field convention for invariant polynomials matches the supplied real or complex G-reduction. The proof uses polarization only over that Lie algebra's scalar field; its covariant derivative and transgression identity remain licensed.

The determinant coefficients use complex-coordinate polynomials on gl over C, while the real connection's complexification uses those same coefficients and the Pfaffian uses a real so polynomial. Each is within the revised invariant-polynomial domain; the displayed reality and transgression arguments are unchanged.

The changed étale definition keeps the smooth relative-dimension-zero criterion and merely corrects its example and fibre terminology. This neighbourhood definition uses only the morphism-wide étale predicate and the residue-field isomorphism, both still valid.

The locus uses étaleness at a point and its germ locality. The revised supplier still defines that as smoothness with relative dimension zero, so the subset identity, smooth-locus inclusion and empty-source case remain accurate.

Its parameter reversal pairs each of the two marked bigon corners with itself. The round disk conjugation carries those marked points to diameter endpoints, so the corrected corner-preserving schema requirement is satisfied and the sphere quotient calculation stands.

Its actual schema use is the quotient of finitely many convex polygon faces along full subdivided edges. The face pairing maps their endpoint vertices to endpoint vertices, so the newly explicit marked-corner condition holds without altering the triangulation construction.

The corrected L5 includes the disk, bigon and monogon schema convention. The proof actually builds a straight-edge polygon by attaching finitely many triangles; its remaining paired sides match their marked endpoints affinely, so no new corner mismatch arises.

L2 incorrectly described every one-face schema as a straight-edge polygon although the theorem explicitly retains the permitted sphere bigon. I changed only that fact to include a polygon or bigon disk; side-pairing corner counts and the Statement are unchanged.

The classification proof uses the sphere bigon and finite paired polygon words from normal form. Their pairing maps marked side endpoints to marked endpoints, including its slit construction, so the schema definition change does not invalidate its connected-sum or cell-count uses.

The corrected covering-atlas definition still supplies local chart discs, but proof 1.1 chose one disc at every point while claiming no choice. It now takes all admissible chart-disc triples as an open cover and extracts a finite subcover, preserving the choice-free triangulation claim.

The supplier now explicitly requires the atlas to cover X, which this theorem already uses to orient every point. Biholomorphic chart transitions have positive real Jacobian and the compact connected surface classification applies; the finite chart triangulation proof was repaired without changing its Statement.

Its compact Riemann surface satisfies the corrected covering-atlas requirement. The genus is still the unique handle number given by classification, and the finite Euler cell count still equals 2 minus twice genus, including the sphere digon case.

The revised Schwartz multiplier defines its output through a tempered extension of the compact-test distribution. This definition explicitly requires every Schwartz input to belong to that domain and to have an Lp regular output, so its density-based bounded extension remains well typed.

The direct-integral correction integrates real and imaginary components of fibre pairings. This operator-field definition uses the resulting complex Hilbert quotient, and its weak-measurability condition supplies measurable norms before essential boundedness is defined; no additional change is needed.

The repaired covering-atlas interface supplies connected chart restrictions, and the corrected meromorphic-map domain convention applies on their plane-domain images. The transition law is checked componentwise, so order and residue remain chart independent without invoking a meromorphic function on a disconnected domain.

Both oracle tables have 2 to a nonnegative power coordinates, including one coordinate at dimension zero, so they satisfy the revised nonempty distance domain. The arbitrary-matrix satisfaction formula already uses the full tensor dot product and remains well defined.

The reduction writes every gate equation in canonical upper-triangular form, placing linear terms on the diagonal and products above it. The revised full ordered-pair satisfaction formula agrees with that form, so the fixed-prefix solution equivalence is unchanged.

The two Walsh-Hadamard tables always share the nonempty cube coordinate set of size 2^n. Pairing each mask with its translate by a coordinate where u+v is one gives exactly half the entries different; the n=0 boundary has no distinct messages.

Every distance used by the BLR decoder is between tables on the same cube, whose size 2^n is positive even for n=0. The Fourier maximizer and the half-distance uniqueness argument therefore remain within the corrected distance definition.

This lemma explicitly assumes a canonical instance; the revised full ordered-pair tensor formula agrees with its matrix dot product. For a violated assignment the nonzero residual vector is detected on exactly half of masks, and the two-query error bound remains licensed.

The f and g distances are on cubes of sizes 2^N and 2^(N squared), both nonzero, so the corrected distance domain is satisfied. Row-major tensor coordinates and the ideal bilinear comparison are unchanged; the N=0 unequal-tensor premise is impossible.

The Statement admits arbitrary QUADEQ matrices, but its Given and random-subsum supplier required canonical matrices. Proof 1.1 now canonicalizes every input by adding paired off-diagonal entries, preserving each quadratic value in O(MN squared) time before the canonical test is invoked.

Its two proof tables have 2^n1 and 2^n2 entries and hence nonempty coordinate sets, so proximity distances remain defined at zero dimensions. The interface does not claim that its raw slice check alone proves proximity; the separate BLR checks in the construction remain required.

The corrected symmetric-algebra definition already derives the base-change map from the tensor quotient universal property. This lemma supplies the same isomorphism via explicit inverse maps and affine sheaf gluing, so its Statement and proof remain licensed.

The base-change remark attributed arbitrary relative Proj base change to a construction that proves affine restriction only. Added the existing relative Proj base-change theorem to that remark and the dependency lists; symmetric-algebra base change remains separately cited. The Definition section is unchanged.

Its robust block coordinates are Walsh-Hadamard tables on full Boolean cubes, with positive sizes 2^n even at n=0. Every relative distance in the block definition therefore satisfies the corrected nonempty-coordinate hypothesis.

The corrected differential theorem supplies local freeness on the smooth locus; this definition assumes X smooth everywhere of pure relative dimension n. Thus the top exterior power is still invertible and the projective-space and trace conventions remain in their stated domain.

The changed étale definition retains smooth relative dimension zero. A monic one-equation presentation localized where P prime is invertible has finite presentation and an invertible one-by-one Jacobian, so its asserted étale example remains valid.

F4 imports the revised invariant-polynomial convention: complex-coordinate polynomials use complex polarization, while a complex group treated as real permits real-coordinate polynomials and real polarization. The product-polarization formula and even-form commutativity use only the supplied scalar field, so the map remains valid.

Its relative affine spectrum is built from the symmetric algebra and its universal property. The corrected gluing map and base-change identity in the supplier supply exactly the algebra transition maps used here; no vector-bundle clause requires alteration.

The supplier now justifies complex inner-product integrals by separately integrable real and imaginary components. This completeness proof uses that same quotient inner product and nonnegative squared norm; its Cauchy-sequence and measurable-limit construction do not assume a real L1 quotient for complex pairings.

For a constant fibre the direct-integral quotient identifies section classes pointwise with complex L2 classes. The corrected componentwise integral of complex inner products gives the usual L2 inner product, so the example and its null-set convention remain accurate.

The theorem starts with weakly measurable operator fields, exactly the new premise under which the supplier proves measurability of their norms. The fibre norm bound and measurable-section pairing then give a well-defined bounded action on the corrected complex direct integral.

The commutant construction produces fields whose fundamental coefficients are measurable before applying essential norm bounds. Its null-set gluing uses the direct-integral quotient, and its uniqueness argument tests a countable dense family; both uses remain licensed by the corrected supplier definitions.

The scalar and rank-one fields in this proof have measurable fundamental coefficients, so the qualified norm measurability and essential supremum definitions apply. Pointwise field operations descend through the corrected direct-integral null quotient without a new assumption.

The model uses an explicitly measurable Hilbert field and invokes only weakly measurable, essentially bounded decomposable operators through the commutant theorem. The corrected norm qualification and complex direct-integral pairing therefore preserve the spectral representation interface.

For the constant two-dimensional field, fundamental coefficients are exactly the four Borel matrix entries. Their measurability is established before the essential operator norm is used, and the finite-entry bound yields the corrected decomposability criterion.

Its four entries are explicit Borel functions of t, so the field is weakly measurable before its norm and essential supremum are evaluated. The corrected operator-field definition applies, and the resulting fibrewise action is still well defined on direct-integral classes.

The example computes a two-member affine cover of nonempty projective line. The supplier correction concerns the empty-scheme cover boundary, while its ordinary Čech comparison and explicit Laurent cocycle calculation remain valid here.

The quotient charts constructed from lattice translates cover every coset, so they meet the corrected atlas covering requirement. Translation transitions are holomorphic with nonzero derivative; compactness, connectedness and Hausdorffness arguments do not rely on a noncovering atlas.

The short and long Walsh-Hadamard tables live on full cubes of sizes 2^n and 2^N, both positive even when n=0. The half-mask disagreement and four-query union bound therefore use relative distance only within its revised nonempty domain.

Its circuit reduction produces canonical QUADEQ matrices, which satisfy the corrected full ordered-pair tensor equation exactly. All private and proximity tables have positive cube sizes, so the nonempty distance condition is met, including zero-dimensional prefixes.

The example uses one-dimensional Walsh-Hadamard tables with two indexed coordinates and exact linear values. Its composition witness never invokes distance on an empty set, so the revised domain restriction does not affect its perfect-completeness calculation.

The covering atlas supplies a connected chart around each point, and the repaired differential definition gives meromorphic coefficients there. The proof places finitely many poles in chart-cell interiors and cancels paired edge integrals using the componentwise transition law; these uses remain licensed.

Its coordinate changes are between connected local chart domains, so the corrected meromorphic differential family includes both coefficients. The chain-rule transition preserves the Laurent order and residue as calculated; no disconnected-chart assertion is used.

The revised étale definition retains smoothness of relative dimension zero. For a finite field extension, flatness and finite presentation hold, and separability is exactly the reduced geometric-fibre condition used through the flat-unramified criterion; the degree-two case is not excluded.

The theorem uses a finite standard affine cover of projective space and its nonempty intersections. The corrected Čech theorem still identifies that complex with sheaf cohomology; its added empty-scheme boundary clause does not alter the finite-generation or vanishing argument.

The extension cocycle is computed on the two nonempty standard affine charts of P1 over k[a]. The Čech supplier change only corrects its empty-scheme cover convention; the fibre H1 generator and jumping H0 calculation remain valid.

This example imports the explicit rank-two extension and fibre sequence from the preceding example, whose own Statement is unchanged. The two nonempty P1 charts and long exact cohomology sequence still give constant Euler characteristic with jumping H0 and H1.
